h: The Great Shofar Restores the Lost and Dispersed

p: The haftarah of this parashah closes
He has comforted all her ruins,
and He has made her wilderness like Eden
and her desert like the garden of Hashem";
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (שָׁם כז, יג)
"And it will be on that day:
a great shofar will be sounded,
and those lost in the land of Ashur will come,
and those cast away in the land of Egypt," etc.
alludes to the middah of Binah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב מו, ב
That is, the shofar indicates fear,
"If a shofar is sounded in a city,
that they have no fear of Heaven.
(in the Rema at the beginning of Orach Chaim):
stands over him and sees his deeds,
fear will immediately come to him," etc.
and this is when fear enters
into the depths of the heart,
"Then you will understand the fear of Hashem," etc.;
and this is called the great shofar.
"and those lost in the land of Ashur will come":
these are the ones who assimilated completely
and do not know their root at all,
the great shofar will awaken fear,
and through this they will return to Hashem.
"And those cast away in the land of Egypt":
that is, they know their root,
only through the leaven in the dough
they are cast away from holiness
like a fetus in its mother's womb,
And that is why it says,
He has comforted all her ruins":
the lost and the cast away.
And that is why it says,
corresponding to "those lost in the land of Ashur,"
who assimilated completely among the nations,
and they are called by the name wilderness,
He will make it like Eden:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר (תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן נה, פח, א)
"And Eden is none other than Kesser Elyon."
from the aspect of Kesser Elyon,
along the lines of what it says (Shabbos 89b):
אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח)
like these years that are arrayed and come
from the six days of Creation," etc.
which alludes to the deeds of the wicked;
over the face of the waters":
and Hashem Yisbarach will make clear about them
alludes to "those cast away in the land of Egypt,"
and they need "the garden of Hashem,"
"And his heart will understand, and he will return."
And it is called "the garden of Hashem,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קפב, ב)
along the lines of what it says (Zohar III 182b):
is called a garden relative to the Eden above," etc.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א כו, א)
and as it says (Zohar III, ibid.):
is the aspect of the holy Field of Apples,
and through the arousal from below,
they will merit the great shofar,
"Joy and gladness will be found in her":
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
which is the Shabbos of Shabbos eve,
that is, through the arousal from below
And when one merits the upper Shabbos,
"and to make for them a dwelling
in the two chambers of the heart,"
אָז אִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִן תַּמָּן
then "the yetzer hara is cleared out from there"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן מח, פה, א)
and one merits to straighten the heart,
and through this one comes to joy,
"And for the upright of heart, joy";
and this comes as a find
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עא)
according to what it says (Bereishis Rabbah 71):
this one gives me of his own;
לְפִיכָךְ אֲנִי מַחֲזִיק לוֹ טוֹבָה וְכוּלֵּי
therefore I am grateful to him," etc.;
"and once Leah bore a fourth son,
she said: This time I will thank," etc.
That is, when one is given
when it comes as a find,
And in "A song for thanksgiving" it says (Tehillim 100:2):
come before Him with joyous song":
which is "for the upright of heart, joy,"
when one merits the upper Shabbos,
then "come before Him with joyous song."
And that is why it says,
וּבְמִזְמוֹר דְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת כְּתִיב (שָׁם צב, ב)
And in the psalm of the Shabbos day it is written (ibid. 92:2):
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem
and to sing to Your Name, O Most High":
"Most High" indicates the middah of Atika;
that is, on Shabbos one merits
and when one merits the upper Shabbos,
and the yetzer hara is cleared out from there,
there come "thanksgiving and the sound of song."
And then one merits to rectify at the root,
"like these years that are arrayed and come
from the six days of Creation,"
then "they will become white as snow":
for so it arose in thought before Him
at the creation of the world,
except that which comes out of darkness,
except that which comes out of evil"
